all of that. And I actually paid someone else, so I needed a bit of money. And we got our first internet page up, or website, shall I say. And after a few days, it was doing quite well. It wasn't selling. There was no e-commerce on there. It was purely to get people to the shop to see what we sold, so they could phone us, email us, and all that sort of thing. But within about two years, that was 50% of my business was online. Now, all my other friends were opening up multiple shops, going to different locations, and they thought they were doing all right. And for a time, they were, until they weren't, until the high street started backing away. Because what I'd seen was the opportunities were where the customers were going to be. Not where they'd been for 50 years, that was changing. It's where they're going to be. And I think that's always worth having that in mind, where are your customers going to be in the future? And I think there's two very important lessons, and I think it's like... Thank you.
